pages.text: Young rice plants lay in a bamboo basket for Dingding's field. One bundle for each row.
Grandma counted duck eggs, setting one stone for each. Tap, tap, tap.
"How many bundles, Mom?" She glanced across the field. "I will count."
"One, two, three, four..." Ducks quacked below. Mom turned sharply.
"Where was I? Five?" She started again.
Her basket kept slipping. She adjusted it on her head. "Six bundles! Exactly six."
Dingding planted all six. But one side of the field stayed empty.
Dingding gathered bank stones, placing one for each row. Tap, tap, tap.
Nine stones! "Nine rows! We need three more bundles."
Mom brought another bamboo basket. "My fingers must keep wandering." Beside Grandma lay a heap of stones.
